Fortson, stationed at nearby NAS Pensacola, was shot in May 2023 during a welfare check at his Fort Walton Beach home. The…
item.content:encoded:
A courtroom packed with supporters of Roger Fortson heard the opening of testimony Wednesday in the case against former Okaloosa County Deputy Eddie Duran, who is charged in connection with the death of the Air Force airman.

Fortson, stationed at nearby NAS Pensacola, was shot in May 2023 during a welfare check at his Fort Walton Beach home. The case has drawn significant community attention and support for Fortson's family.

Duran, a former member of the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office, faces charges stemming from the shooting. The trial is underway in Okaloosa County, which borders Santa Rosa County to the west of Escambia.

item.content:encoded:
Testimony got underway Tuesday in the case of Roger Fortson, an Air Force airman killed by former Okaloosa County Deputy Eddie Duran. The courtroom was packed with supporters of Fortson as prosecutors and the defense presented their opening cases and called nine witnesses to the stand on the first day of trial.

Fortson's death has drawn significant attention both locally and within military circles, with community members showing up to follow the proceedings. The trial marks a major development in a case that has raised questions about use-of-force policies and law enforcement training in the region.

Further details about witness testimony and the case's trajectory are expected to emerge as the trial continues.

item.title: Alabama I-10 Bridge Project Breaks Ground Near Pensacola Region
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A long-awaited replacement of the aging I-10 bridge across the Mobile River in Baldwin County is set to begin construction next month, with a groundbreaking ceremony planned for Friday, according to WKRG News 5. The multi-billion-dollar project represents decades of planning and could significantly affect traffic patterns for drivers throughout…
item.content:encoded:
A long-awaited replacement of the aging I-10 bridge across the Mobile River in Baldwin County is set to begin construction next month, with a groundbreaking ceremony planned for Friday, according to WKRG News 5. The multi-billion-dollar project represents decades of planning and could significantly affect traffic patterns for drivers throughout the region, including those traveling between Pensacola and points east.

The new bridge is expected to ease congestion on one of the Gulf Coast's most critical transportation corridors. The current structure has been a bottleneck for commuters and commercial traffic for years, and the replacement is anticipated to improve flow across the Mobile River when completed.

The project's start date comes after years of discussion and planning among state and local officials in Alabama. While the work is centered in Baldwin County, the improved infrastructure could have ripple effects on traffic conditions for Northwest Florida drivers who regularly use I-10 to travel toward the Mobile area and beyond.

item.title: Florida Turnpike Expansion Hits 55% Complete With $20B Widening Plan
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced progress on a major statewide infrastructure initiative today, highlighting more than $20 billion in investments to widen Florida's Turnpike along its entire 320-mile mainline stretching from South Florida through Central Florida to Interstate 75 near Wildwood. According to the Florida Department of Transportation,…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced progress on a major statewide infrastructure initiative today, highlighting more than $20 billion in investments to widen Florida's Turnpike along its entire 320-mile mainline stretching from South Florida through Central Florida to Interstate 75 near Wildwood.

According to the Florida Department of Transportation, the widening project is currently 55 percent complete and will eventually expand every section of the mainline to six or more lanes. Once finished, the improvements are expected to add more than 965 lane miles of capacity to reduce congestion across one of Florida's busiest corridors. To date, FDOT has already added 384 lane miles across the Turnpike system, including 179 miles along the mainline itself.

Beyond roadway expansion, the state is also investing in traveler amenities and commercial driver support. FDOT announced nearly $8.5 million to refresh food options and amenities at service plazas, with new vendors including Jimmy John's, Zaxby's, and Villa Pizza now open at multiple locations. An additional $53.8 million will expand truck parking at Turkey Lake and Ocoee Service Plazas, adding nearly 150 parking spaces to support commercial drivers.

Recent completed sections include a widening project between State Road 50 in Clermont and Hancock Road in Minneola, finished in June 2026, and a stretch from Northwest 106th Street to I-75 in Miami-Dade County that recently opened to traffic. FDOT Secretary Jared Perdue noted that transportation infrastructure improvements directly support Florida's quality of life by connecting residents to jobs and economic opportunities.

item.title: West Roberts Road to Close Sept. 30 for Drainage Work
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County will temporarily close a section of West Roberts Road between Stallion Road and Pine Forest Road beginning Wednesday, Sept. 30, as part of ongoing roadway reconstruction and drainage improvements. The closure is expected to last through Saturday, Oct. 3, weather permitting. Drivers should anticipate intermittent lane closures along…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County will temporarily close a section of West Roberts Road between Stallion Road and Pine Forest Road beginning Wednesday, Sept. 30, as part of ongoing roadway reconstruction and drainage improvements. The closure is expected to last through Saturday, Oct. 3, weather permitting.

Drivers should anticipate intermittent lane closures along the entire West Roberts Road corridor for the duration of the project. County officials are directing traffic to use detours via Kingsfield Road, Stallion Road, and Tate Road. Authorities ask that drivers exercise caution, follow posted signs, and heed instructions from road crews working in the area.

Property access will be maintained for residents and emergency vehicles throughout construction, though driveways and entrances may be briefly blocked as crews move equipment and materials. The overall West Roberts Road Roadway and Drainage Improvements Project is slated for completion by fall 2026, pending weather and construction scheduling.

item.content:encoded:
Three loggerhead sea turtles are swimming free again in the Gulf of Mexico after recovering from injuries sustained at Gulf State Park Pier earlier this month, according to WKRG News 5.

The turtles had been hooked while in the pier area and were brought in for rehabilitation. After treatment and recovery, they were deemed healthy enough to return to their natural habitat.

The release marks a successful outcome for the marine wildlife rehabilitation effort, though details on the specific injuries and treatment timeline were not immediately available.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Outlines 'Rescue America' Plan on Senate Floor
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott took to the Senate floor today to present his "Rescuing America" plan, which focuses on addressing what he calls the nation's affordability crisis and the rise of socialism. The plan centers on three core initiatives: balancing the federal budget, cutting government regulations, and boosting private sector job creation.…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott took to the Senate floor today to present his "Rescuing America" plan, which focuses on addressing what he calls the nation's affordability crisis and the rise of socialism. The plan centers on three core initiatives: balancing the federal budget, cutting government regulations, and boosting private sector job creation.

Scott argued that Congress bears responsibility for current economic challenges, citing a "$40 trillion debt bomb" created by federal government expansion and massive spending bills that he says have driven up prices and interest rates. He contended that widespread anger among Americans stems from the erosion of the American Dream, particularly for younger generations facing affordability challenges.

The senator framed his proposal as an alternative to what he characterized as the appeal of socialism among voters frustrated with the status quo. Scott said the solutions, while simple in concept, require political will—suggesting the budget could be balanced and federal regulations cut in half by year's end if lawmakers commit to the effort. His remarks emphasized the need to "blow up the status quo in Washington" through tax cuts, smart investment, and focused economic policy.

item.content:encoded:
A funk-rock band with influences ranging from reggae to jam takes the stage tonight at Pensacola Beach as part of the free outdoor summer concert series. Float Like a Buffalo performs from 7 to 9 p.m. at the Gulfside Pavilion at Casino Beach, according to the Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce.

The band draws from artists like Lettuce, The Motet, Pigeons Playing Ping Pong, and James Brown—combining rock, funk, ska, reggae, and jam into what organizers describe as high-energy performances that inspire dancing. The show overlooks the Gulf of Mexico.

Attendees are encouraged to bring their own lawn chairs and blankets. Pets and glass containers are prohibited. For updates, call the Santa Rosa Island Authority at (850) 932-2257 or tune to Cat Country 98.7.

Details on the specific timeline, financial terms, and impact on customer accounts and branches have not yet been disclosed. The credit union said it would provide more information as the transaction moves forward.

item.title: USPS Releases Hanukkah Dreidel Stamp; Ceremony Held in Historic Jewish Synagogue
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service unveiled its ninth Hanukkah commemorative stamp today, featuring a colorful digital illustration of a dreidel set against a turquoise background with decorative floral elements. The stamp was dedicated at the Touro Synagogue in a ceremony that highlighted the holiday's roots in religious freedom and resilience. The dreidel…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service unveiled its ninth Hanukkah commemorative stamp today, featuring a colorful digital illustration of a dreidel set against a turquoise background with decorative floral elements. The stamp was dedicated at the Touro Synagogue in a ceremony that highlighted the holiday's roots in religious freedom and resilience.

The dreidel design, created by illustrator Lisa Perrin under USPS art director Antonio Alcalá, depicts the four-sided spinning top with Hebrew letters — nun, gimel, heh, and shin — that together spell "A great miracle happened there," referencing the Hanukkah legend of oil that burned for eight days during the rededication of the Jewish Temple around 167 B.C. "The Postal Service takes immense pride in issuing stamps that celebrate the rich cultural traditions and shared history of the American people," said Deputy General Counsel Carrie Rieger Brownlie at the ceremony.

The new Hanukkah stamp is being issued as a Forever stamp in panes of 20, meaning it will always be valid for current First-Class Mail postage. The stamps are available for purchase through USPS's online store, by phone at (844) 737-7824, by mail through USA Philatelic, or at post office locations nationwide.

item.title: Three Santa Rosa Deputies Injured in Gulf Breeze Pursuit, Suspect Detained
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 26-year-old man is in custody after leading Santa Rosa County Sheriff's deputies on a chase that left three officers injured Tuesday morning. John Charles Newell III was driving a white U-Haul pickup truck through residential lawns on Tibet Drive in Gulf Breeze around 11:22 a.m. when deputies arrived to investigate, according to a sheriff's…
item.content:encoded:
A 26-year-old man is in custody after leading Santa Rosa County Sheriff's deputies on a chase that left three officers injured Tuesday morning. John Charles Newell III was driving a white U-Haul pickup truck through residential lawns on Tibet Drive in Gulf Breeze around 11:22 a.m. when deputies arrived to investigate, according to a sheriff's office news release.

When deputies made contact with Newell, he drove away from the scene, injuring officers in the process and prompting a pursuit. During the chase, Newell rammed a deputy's vehicle near Highway 98 and Kell Road, disabling that patrol car and injuring the deputy inside. The U-Haul eventually lost control on East Bay Boulevard, where Newell abandoned the truck and fled on foot before being apprehended by responding deputies.

All three injured deputies were transported to a local hospital and are listed in stable condition, the sheriff's office said. The incident remains under investigation, with additional details expected as the case develops.

item.title: DeSantis Cabinet approves conservation of 10,770 acres across Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet on Tuesday approved the conservation of more than 10,770 acres statewide, with more than 2,700 acres designated within the Ocala-to-Osceola Wildlife Corridor. The projects represent a combined investment of $72.6 million and advance three state conservation initiatives: Florida Forever, the Rural and…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet on Tuesday approved the conservation of more than 10,770 acres statewide, with more than 2,700 acres designated within the Ocala-to-Osceola Wildlife Corridor. The projects represent a combined investment of $72.6 million and advance three state conservation initiatives: Florida Forever, the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, and habitat connectivity efforts.

Among the approved acquisitions are a 2,708-acre conservation easement in Putnam County that will connect existing conservation lands within the Ocala-to-Osceola corridor, safeguarding regional water supply and flood protection. A second 3,567-acre easement in Hendry County will link the Dinner Island Ranch Wildlife Management Area to other protected lands while preserving agricultural operations. The state also approved permanent conservation easements on more than 4,500 acres of working farmland through the agricultural lands protection program, including a 1,034-acre cattle ranch in operation for more than 70 years.

Since 2019, Florida has invested more than $1.5 billion in land conservation, acquiring over 500,000 acres — 92 percent within the Florida Wildlife Corridor. State officials said the latest approvals balance growth with preservation and support ecosystem functions including wildlife habitat protection and aquifer recharge.

item.title: DeSantis announces $20B Florida Turnpike expansion, service plaza upgrades
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced a more than $20 billion investment Tuesday to widen Florida's Turnpike across its entire 320-mile mainline from South Florida through Central Florida to Interstate 75 in Wildwood, according to the Governor's Press Office. The project, which is currently 55 percent complete, will expand every section of the mainline…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced a more than $20 billion investment Tuesday to widen Florida's Turnpike across its entire 320-mile mainline from South Florida through Central Florida to Interstate 75 in Wildwood, according to the Governor's Press Office.

The project, which is currently 55 percent complete, will expand every section of the mainline to six or more lanes, adding more than 965 lane miles of capacity statewide. Under DeSantis' administration, the Florida Department of Transportation has already added 384 lane miles across Florida's Turnpike System, including 179 along the mainline. Recent completed sections include the widening from State Road 50 in Clermont to Hancock Road in Minneola, finished in June 2026, and the section from the Dolphin Expressway to Northwest 106th Street in Miami-Dade County, completed in February 2024.

Beyond mainline expansion, FDOT announced nearly $8.5 million for new food concepts and customer service improvements at Turnpike service plazas, including renovated areas with Jimmy John's, Zaxby's, Villa Pizza, and Vending Oasis locations. The state also earmarked nearly $54 million to expand truck parking at the system, with a $53.8 million investment specifically improving roughly 150 parking spaces at Turkey Lake and Ocoee Service Plazas to support commercial drivers and Florida's supply chain.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Air Show Generated $38.8M in Economic Impact in 2026
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Air Show proved to be a major draw for the regional economy this year, generating an estimated $38.8 million in economic impact across the Pensacola area, according to a study by Downs & St. Germain Research commissioned by Visit Pensacola. The 2026 show attracted 206,700 total attendees, with 133,500 unique visitors after…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Air Show proved to be a major draw for the regional economy this year, generating an estimated $38.8 million in economic impact across the Pensacola area, according to a study by Downs & St. Germain Research commissioned by Visit Pensacola.

The 2026 show attracted 206,700 total attendees, with 133,500 unique visitors after accounting for repeat attendance across multiple days. Of those, 73,500 came from outside Escambia County and spent $25.42 million on hotels, restaurants, shopping, attractions, and other expenses. The out-of-county visitors generated 41,300 paid lodging nights throughout the area, with a typical travel party of 3.4 people staying an average of 2.3 nights and spending about $1,180 per person.

Perhaps most significantly, 70 percent of out-of-county visitors identified the Air Show as their primary reason for visiting the Pensacola area. "This air show is an economic driver that reaches far beyond the beach, and these numbers demonstrate just how important this event is to our entire community," said Mike Burns, Executive Director of the Santa Rosa Island Authority.

The event has shown consistent growth in its economic footprint. Last year's air show generated $31.5 million in total impact with $20.6 million in direct visitor spending and 124,000 unique attendees. The economic figures include direct spending plus indirect and induced economic activity generated by tourism dollars, but do not count spending by local residents.

The feedback suggests that the alternate parade route has gained favor among community members, though the full details of the survey and the specific differences between the routes were not immediately available. A decision on whether to formalize the change would likely require approval from city leadership.

item.title: Air Force Reservist pleads guilty to PPP loan fraud scheme
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The guilty plea marks another case in the ongoing federal crackdown on pandemic relief fraud. The Justice Department has pursued hundreds of cases nationwide…
item.content:encoded:
A Navarre man who served as an Air Force Reservist has admitted to wire and loan fraud in federal court related to COVID-era Paycheck Protection Program funds, according to WKRG News 5.

The guilty plea marks another case in the ongoing federal crackdown on pandemic relief fraud. The Justice Department has pursued hundreds of cases nationwide involving misuse of PPP funds that were distributed to help businesses survive pandemic-related shutdowns.

Details on the specific amounts involved or sentencing date were not immediately available.
